declaration.preface:
PennEngineering & Manufacturing Corp. (“PennEngineering”) (Group) is a global manufacturer of engineered fastening solutions and installation systems used in industries such as automotive, electronics, industrial equipment, and telecommunications. Through advanced engineering capabilities and precision manufacturing, the Company develops fastening technologies that support product reliability, efficiency, and performance across diverse industrial applications.

PennEngineering is committed to conducting business with the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and ethical responsibility. The Company recognizes that ethical conduct is fundamental to maintaining the trust of employees, customers, suppliers, shareholders, and the communities in which it operates.
declaration.declaration:
This Business Ethics Roadmap establishes the core principles that guide ethical behavior and responsible decision-making across PennEngineering’s global operations. It reflects the expectations placed on employees, contractors, and business partners in the way business is conducted and decisions are made.

The Roadmap serves as a framework to support compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and internal governance requirements, while promoting fairness, accountability, and transparency in all business activities. As business environments evolve, this Roadmap remains an important reference point to ensure that PennEngineering continues to uphold the highest ethical standards in its operations and relationships.
declaration.scope:
This Business Ethics Roadmap applies to all PennEngineering operations, including manufacturing facilities, engineering centers, offices, and distribution activities globally. The Roadmap applies to all employees, Workers, contractors, suppliers, and other stakeholders involved in the Company’s operations and value chain.

PennEngineering operates in multiple countries with different business operations and regulatory requirements related to ethics. While this roadmap’s vision and objectives apply across all locations, each facility will implement these principles in accordance with local regulations, operational requirements, and internal best practices.

focusAreas: Anti-Bribery, Anti-Corruption and Ethical Business Practices
Conflict of Interest Prevention and Management
Anti-Money Laundering and Responsible Financial Practices

Anti-Bribery, Anti-Corruption and Ethica: PennEngineering strictly prohibits bribery, corruption, facilitation payments, or any form of improper advantage in business dealings. The Company is committed to conducting business fairly and transparently and expects employees and business partners to uphold the highest standards of integrity in all interactions with customers, suppliers, government authorities, and other stakeholders.
Conduct all business with integrity and transparency. Promptly report any suspected bribery or unethical conduct to your manager, General Counsel, or speakup@pemnet.com.
Decline gifts, favours, or benefits that could influence business decisions.
Do not offer, accept, or solicit bribes, kickbacks, facilitation payments, or improper advantages. Do not tolerate corruption or unethical behaviour, even if local custom allows it.
Do not conceal or ignore suspected bribery or corruption.
Conflict of Interest Prevention and Mana: PennEngineering expects employees to act in the best interests of the Company and avoid situations where personal, financial, or external interests may conflict with business responsibilities. Employees are encouraged to disclose any potential or actual conflicts of interest so that appropriate measures can be taken to manage and resolve them transparently.
Disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest immediately.
Obtain approval before engaging in external employment or business activities that may conflict with company interests.
Follow internal reporting and resolution processes for conflicts.
Do not make business decisions for personal gain or to benefit family/friends.
Do not engage in unauthorized dealings with competitors, suppliers, or customers.
Do not misuse company resources or confidential information for personal advantage.
Anti-Money Laundering and Responsible Fi: PennEngineering is committed to preventing money laundering and ensuring that all financial transactions are legitimate, transparent, and properly documented. The Company complies with applicable financial regulations and maintains strong internal controls to safeguard financial integrity and prevent the misuse of company resources.
Report suspicious or unusual financial activities to the Compliance or Finance team.
Conduct due diligence on customers, suppliers, and partners.
Maintain verifiable records of all financial transactions.
Do not approve transactions without legitimate business purpose.
Do not ignore warning signs such as unexplained payments or high-risk transactions.
Do not participate in activities intended to disguise the origin of funds.
Data Accuracy and Ethical Reporting: PennEngineering promotes accuracy, honesty, and transparency in all business records and reporting activities. Employees are expected to maintain complete and accurate documentation of financial transactions, operational data, and business communications in accordance with applicable accounting standards and internal governance procedures.
Ensure all financial and operational reports are accurate, complete, and timely.
Cooperate fully with audits and data verification processes.
Maintain proper documentation to support reporting.
Do not provide false, incomplete, or misleading data.
Do not manipulate reports to meet targets.
Do not destroy records relevant to audits or investigations.
Fair Competition and Market Integrity: PennEngineering supports fair and open competition in all markets where it operates. The Company complies with applicable competition and antitrust laws and avoids any agreements or practices that could restrict fair competition, such as price fixing, market allocation, or collusive bidding.
Compete fairly and ethically in pricing, bidding, and market activities.
Comply with all applicable competition and antitrust laws.
Seek guidance when engaging in competitor interactions.
Do not engage in price-fixing, bid-rigging, collusion, or market allocation.
Do not share sensitive commercial information with competitors.
Do not abuse market position to restrict fair competition.
Fraud Prevention and Financial Integrity: PennEngineering works to prevent, detect, and address fraudulent activities through appropriate internal controls, monitoring systems, and reporting mechanisms. Employees are encouraged to report suspected fraud or unethical conduct through established reporting channels so that appropriate investigations and corrective actions can be taken.
Report suspected fraud or financial misconduct immediately.
Follow internal controls and company procedures diligently.
Ensure transparency and accuracy in all financial records.
Do not falsify accounts, invoices, or expense reports.
Do not manipulate financial statements for personal or departmental gain.
Information Security and Data Privacy: PennEngineering recognizes the importance of protecting confidential information and personal data belonging to employees, customers, and business partners. The Company implements appropriate information security practices and complies with applicable data protection and privacy laws to safeguard sensitive information from unauthorized access, disclosure, or misuse.
Follow all IT, cybersecurity, and data protection policies.
Use strong passwords, approved devices, and security controls.
Immediately report data breaches, phishing attempts, or unauthorized access.
Do not disclose confidential or personal data without authorization.
Do not use unapproved devices or platforms for sensitive data.
Do not bypass security controls or share access credentials.

policy.monitoring:
PennEngineering is committed to actively monitoring adherence to its Business Ethics Roadmap and tracking progress toward its ethical objectives and compliance targets. Key performance indicators (KPIs) — including employee ethics training completion, compliance audit results, incident and whistleblower reports, ethical decision-making metrics, and adherence to legal and company standards — are regularly tracked across all operational sites.

The Compliance Officer is responsible for collecting, analysing, and reviewing ethics-related performance data. This data is used to assess progress, identify improvement opportunities, and ensure ongoing compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and company policies.

PennEngineering conducts periodic reviews of business ethics performance through internal audits, management assessments, employee feedback mechanisms, and compliance evaluations. Where appropriate, ethics-related information may also be shared externally through sustainability reports, customer assessments, or other reporting frameworks.

Through systematic monitoring, transparent communication, and continuous improvement, PennEngineering aims to strengthen accountability, promote ethical business conduct, and uphold integrity across all operations.
policy.reviewMechanism:
The Compliance Officer is responsible for conducting an annual review of the Business Ethics Roadmap. This review assesses the Roadmap’s effectiveness, progress toward ethics-related objectives and targets, and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and internationally recognized standards for ethical business conduct.

Any updates or revisions resulting from organizational changes, regulatory developments, or stakeholder feedback will be incorporated into the Roadmap and communicated across relevant operational sites. This process ensures that the Roadmap remains current, effective, and aligned with PennEngineering’s commitment to ethical business practices, integrity, and responsible corporate governance throughout its operations.
